text.text_excerpt: I've been going over to Hollygrove since they opened. It's great to see that they've expanded, but haven't veered off their mission. It's still $25 for a "box" of fresh and local veggies and fruits. The produce changes weekly and there's always something a little funky (okra or heirloom eggplants or figs, etc.) that you can experiment with in your next week of cooking. They also sell locally sourced cheese, other dairy and meats...but these things are not cheap! (You get what you pay for though!!) The building is surrounded by a community garden and on weekends, a vendor comes to sell fresh shrimp/fish. You can also pick up some local honey and jam. It's atypical from other farmers market...

I love Hollygrove Market. It has become somewhat of a Saturday morning ritual for me. For $25 you get two grocery bags chock-full of fresh produce. I always check out their blog and website to see what the "box" will have before I go. If you're looking to add more plants to your diet, the box is a great route to go. Their blog also provides recipes for the veggies/fruits you might not know what to do with, so it's a good way to branch out if your cooking is in a rut. Last week they had fresh-picked, perfectly ripe strawberries. So good.

I love Hollygrove market and farm! The people here really care about the neighborhood and the food they supply. I love the box. For $25 you get a good amount of really fresh organic produce. I have a bunch of weird allergies (Jalapenos I love you from afar) and they allow substitutions (more satsumas? OMG YES!) if you ask. I like to peruse their clearance table. Bib lettuce for $1 because it has one wilted leaf? Woot! They also tend to have stuff that places like rouses tend not to stock. This is the only place besides hong kong market that I've found persimmons and daikon. The Things love seeing "big gardens" and on slow days they'll even give the kids a mini tour.
